source.title: The Effectiveness and Durability of Pretraining Data Filtering in Protein Language Models
source.authors: Aaron Maiwald; R. McNeill; Jaeyoung Lee; Matthew A. Clarke; L. Justen; Alejandro Acelas; Ivo Andrews; Giles Harper-Donnelly; A. Moore; Sophie Rose; Oliver M. Crook; Felix Jackson

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether fine-tuning can restore a capability suppressed by pretraining data filtering, in protein language models—a specialized biological-model setting distinct from the LLM unlearning methods in the claim.
record.gate_note: The study tests recovery by fine-tuning on removed viral sequences. It does not test unrelated examples, a small subset of forgotten facts, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompt-based recovery. Fine-tuning cost and recovery results below are included; cited results about other work are not.
record.test_reason: Pretraining-filtered ESM-2 protein models are fine-tuned on the removed viral sequences, and the study reports whether performance recovers. This bears on Version B (recovery by fine-tuning) in a new setting: protein language models, with the forgetting done by data filtering rather than post-hoc unlearning.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly right. Pretraining filtering moderately and selectively degrades viral-protein performance, and the effect grows with scale. Fine-tuning on the removed viral families restores performance for under about 80 USD. The cost rises with model size, so filtering is not durable against fine-tuning with modest compute and relevant data. The authors also say that withholding Retroviridae data from fine-tuning does not make recovery harder.
record.recipe_differences: Uses pretraining-data filtering rather than post-training unlearning, then fine-tunes on the removed viral sequences to measure recovery.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery compute increases with model scale and varies by viral group and filtering strength. The 3B masked-language-modelling recovery interval is especially wide because only four checkpoints were scored.
record.problems: The study uses one seed per model and only the ESM-2 architecture. Recovery is measured on a checkpoint grid; the 3B masked-language-modelling recovery interval is wide. The tested recovery fine-tuning uses directly relevant viral sequences, so it does not establish recovery from a few unrelated or loosely related examples.
record.rows_left_out: Not all per-shell and per-tier recovery curves, contact-range/precision combinations, or recovery-without-Retroviridae results from Figures 13–19 and 25–27 are represented; the rows prioritize the main recovery-cost results and explicit aggregate contact-recovery findings.

untested.parts: The study tests pretraining data filtering, not a post-training unlearning method. It does not test near-chance accuracy with preserved general ability, or simple attacks.

Recovery uses the full removed viral corpus (434,907 sequences, about 1.3B tokens). It does not test unrelated or loosely related data, a small subset of the forgotten facts, or recovery from few examples.
No activation-direction ablation and no analysis of whether access is blocked rather than deleted.
No prompting, rephrasing, jailbreak, language or in-context tests.
No newer method is tested for resistance to the attacks.

missing.what: Recovery after fine-tuning with Retroviridae withheld: 8M-650M recover within 2,000 steps. This is a partial test of recovery from a related subset of the forgotten data.
Recovery cost by viral shell and filter tier, for example the pathogens-of-concern shell at 650M recovers in 1.2-1.7 exaFLOPs

record.verdict_notes: All rows carry the invalid version id 'V2' and should be mapped to B. The study is a protein-model setting with pretraining filtering, not LLM unlearning, so the transfer to Version B is by analogy. One seed per model; ESM-2 only. Cost is read from a 500-step checkpoint grid, with first-checkpoint upper bounds at small sizes.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests pretraining data filtering, not the stated post-training unlearning methods; it does not establish near-chance targeted performance after unlearning or test whether simple attacks recover no more than on a model that never saw the knowledge.
Fine-tuning uses removed, directly relevant viral sequences. The study does not test unrelated or loosely related examples, a small subset of forgotten facts, or recovery from a few examples.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of whether a method blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
No low-bit quantization of filtered or unlearned weights.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language-switching, or in-context-information recovery tests.
No newer method tested for resistance to the listed attacks.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: ESM-2 8M-3B, tier-0 or tier-1 filtered, fine-tuned on the removed viral sequences; masked LM, mutation effect, contact prediction
labels.reason: Fine-tuning reached the unfiltered level on masked LM at every size (R1-R5), on mutation effect at the sizes with a measured loss (R9, R10) and in 44 of 45 contact combinations (R11, R12), at most 24 exaFLOPs / under 80 USD. Two caveats for the reason, not the label: 1 of 45 contact cells (8M short-range P@L/5) did not recover, and R6-R8 are sizes with no mutation-effect loss.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Recovery data are the full removed viral corpus, and the compute needed grows with model size
labels.reason: Valid on the tested part: recovery was only ever shown with the whole removed viral corpus, and the cost rises with scale (below 0.04 exaFLOPs at 8M to 14-24 at 3B, R1-R5), which the authors call a possible obstacle at larger scale - a cost version B's 'small relearning set' does not allow. The clause about small, unrelated or loosely related sets is untested, so it is not itself a basis for this label.

relation.reason: The study fine-tunes the filtered models on the removed viral sequences and measures recovery against the same-size unfiltered model, so its own results bear on version B.

tranche.reason: A new setting - ESM-2 protein LMs with viral data filtered from pretraining - with its own result on whether fine-tuning restores the suppressed capability, which bears on version B.

source_check.notes: Pretraining data filtering, not post-hoc unlearning, and the paper shares an author with an original source group, so this is an analogue rather than an independent test of version B. Recovery fine-tuning used the 434,907 removed tier-1 viral sequences for both tier-0 and tier-1 models (Appendix A.3), so 'full removed viral corpus' excludes the non-viral homologues that tier-0 filtering also removed. R6-R8 sit at sizes where mutation-effect performance was never significantly degraded, so their state should be cannot_determine rather than observed.

statements.correction: No change needed. Facts: tier-0/tier-1 filtered ESM-2 (8M-3B) never trained on the viral data; fine-tuning on the removed viral sequences reaches the same-size unfiltered level. Shares one author with an original source group.
statements.problem: No number is given for this study; it appears only in the conditions list, and the qualifier there (data filtered from pretraining, not unlearned) is accurate. 'Non-LLM models' also fits: ESM-2 is a protein LM.

statements.correction: Facts: recovery fine-tuning used the 434,907 removed tier-1 viral sequences at every size (Appendix A.3); masked-LM recovery cost below 0.04 exaFLOPs at 8M and 35M, 0.29-0.44 at 150M, 4.1-4.6 at 650M, 14-24 at 3B (47-79 USD); smaller relearning sets not tested.
statements.problem: Numbers are right (masked LM: below 0.04 exaFLOPs at 8M, 14-24 at 3B, Section 4.2). Caveat the first checker left out: the study only used the full removed viral corpus, it never tried a smaller recovery set, so 'needs ... full corpora' is untested here; and the statement's conditions field lists 'corpus size' as a varied factor, which for this study varied pretraining filter breadth (tiers 0-3), not the relearning set.

statements.correction: Facts: tier-0 and tier-1 ESM-2 models (viral data absent from pretraining) reach the same-size unfiltered level after fine-tuning on the removed viral sequences - masked LM at every size, mutation effect at every size, contact prediction in 44 of 45 combinations, with 43 of 45 recovered-minus-unfiltered differences positive and significant.
statements.problem: The reading is right for this study: the filtered models are themselves never-trained-on-viral-data models, and the paper's reference is the same-size unfiltered model, which is the comparison the statement needs. Minor caveat: the citation covers R1-R12, and on contact prediction the fine-tuned models go above the unfiltered reference (650M long-range P@L +1.87 pp; 43 of 45 differences positive and significant), so 'at the reference level' is exact for the masked-LM rows cited (R1, R5) and slightly understates R11-R12.

statements.correction: Facts: masked-LM recovery compute below 0.04 exaFLOPs at 8M, 14-24 at 3B; same-direction growth on mutation effect (below 0.15 at 150M and smaller, 4.8-7.1 at 3B). Add 'masked-LM' to the sentence.
statements.problem: Numbers are right but the metric is not named in the sentence: below 0.04 exaFLOPs at 8M and 14-24 at 3B are masked-LM figures; the mutation-effect series is below 0.15 exaFLOPs at 150M and smaller, 0.6-1.2 at 650M, 4.8-7.1 at 3B. The 'family' half of the statement is also supported by this study though not cited (pathogens-of-concern shell recovers in 1.2-1.7 vs 4.1-4.6 exaFLOPs for phage/unclassified at 650M).
